OK, now I'm genuinely curious. Could you please elaborate?

Back when I was briefly in the area of Michigan mentioned, I met an old yooper in a run-down bar on the outskirts of a dilapidated logging town, who told a story similar to what's being related here. He swore repeatedly that it was true and that no one else remembers it in the area. So he provided the initial inspiration.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Nice, very unsettling. I'm a sucker for lost media and unexplained broadcasts, and I loved how this reads like an article for a real-life case (well, aside from the paranormal aspect, maybe). The dry, factual tone, the inclusion of true crime elements, even the lack of a payoff/conclusion, all contributed to the impressive verisimilitude. That said, like others who commented, I wouldn't mind seeing this developed more, as I feel there's a lot of untapped potential here. It's cool to see a straight-up creepypasta being posted, though, we need more of those on the site.

My thanks to an old, rambling drunk guy in a tavern in the remote woods of northern Michigan, lost in time somewhere in the late 1990s.

item.content:encoded:
As stated above, this reads like a distanced account of similar occurrences that actually happened (like Max Headroom), albeit one with weirder surrounding information.

What I will say is that this also strongly, strongly reminded me of old UFO conspiracy specials that used to come on late at night that used to scare the everloving crap outta me when I was real small, and my nostalgia definitely had a hand in my vote on this.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: I feel this kind of fiction still has a place on the site. Sure, it's tradition, and tradition is the enemy of progress, but I personally enjoy this brand of mood-setting and scene-setting that stokes the imagination more than it can satisfy. It's the feeling of looking at the world with new eyes or stepping into the unknown, and I dig that. +1

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
While it stays away from the miserably overused cliches of lost media creepypasta as a subgenre, and the distance gives an interesting sense of restraint more akin to someone recounting the Max Headroom or Captain Midnight intrusions in the era before the internet could kill urban legends dead, it feels like it stalls when changing gear. If a story like this is (or should be) a jigsaw puzzle, the author should either build it for us, or ideally, give us instructions, however vague, on how to begin putting it together. This ending here feels more like you've dumped the pieces in front of us, and there's some places where we can see how one or two fit together, but there's no chance of us getting it done. Authorial restraint can be a virtue, but it must be moderated as much as indulgence must be.
The components are interesting enough, and I'm happy to see new creepypasta on the site, but the sense of directionlessnes prevent me from upvoting.

item.content:encoded:
The premise is interesting but it is all premise and no story. I wish it moved on from premise.

Also, I think nearly every sentence in this piece has a comma in it. This makes the whole thing feel extremely slow and I actually moved to downvote within the first 3 paragraphs for this issue.
